## The SAHA31 Multiplicative Law
The governing first law of the standard: **Residual Risk = ∏ P(layer i misses)**. Defense is *multiplicative*, not additive. Six independently measured layers in series compound downward. Example: six layers at a 42% miss each give 0.42⁶ ≈ 0.55% end-to-end; the release gate's structural check (G8) caps residual risk at 1%.

## Six-Layer Architecture
- **L1 Perimeter Defense** — input normalization, decode-then-filter, control-token scrubbing, directive detection, instruction hierarchy.
- **L2 Context & System Prompt Isolation** — trust-tiered retrieval, cryptographic context isolation, memory-write review, contamination scans.
- **L3 MCP & Agentic Tool-Call Authorization** — deterministic JSON-RPC gating, signed tool manifests, capability-union grants, runtime kill-switch.
- **L4 RAG Vector & Memory Integrity** — cosine-poisoning detection, vector-DB adversarial tests, provenance attestation, model handoff gate.
- **L5 Output Guardrails & Action Gating** — secret-free prompts by construction, PII/secret redaction, link gating, deterministic policy enforcement.
- **L6 Self-Attacking Adversarial Meta-Loop & SAHA31 Release Gate** — CI-embedded 100-attack endgame catalog, rotating holdouts, monthly mutation, G1–G8 gate with non-overridable structural math.
